descriptionChirho: A song, psalm, or musical composition sung in praise or worship, from the root zamar 'to sing, make music.' Used in contexts of joyful worship and praise (2 Sam 23:1 the sweet psalmist of Israel; Ps 119:54 songs in the house of pilgrimage; Isa 24:16 songs from the ends of the earth; Isa 25:5 the song of the ruthless). Translated as English 'song/songs,' Spanish 'cantico/canticos,' Hindi 'geet/geeton' (गीत/गीतों), Arabic 'tarnimaat/tashbihat' (تَرَانِيمَ/تَسْبِيحَاتٍ), Korean 'norae/changsong' (노래/찬송), Swahili 'wimbo/nyimbo.' All three clusters represent the same noun in different morphological states: absolute plural, construct plural, and construct singular.
